name: Security
description: Catches the most common and highest-impact security vulnerabilities in web applications. Covers secrets management, injection attacks, authentication, authorization, and data exposure. Suitable for any JavaScript/TypeScript codebase.
author: Solon AI

rules.title: No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or credentials
rules.description: API keys, tokens, passwords, and secrets must never appear in source code. Use environment variables. This includes keys that look like test or placeholder values — they get rotated in but never out.

examples.good: const STRIPE_KEY = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY; const DB_PASSWORD = process.env.DB_PASSWORD;

rules.title: No raw SQL string interpolation
rules.description: Never interpolate user input directly into SQL queries. Use parameterized queries, prepared statements, or an ORM. String-interpolated SQL is the #1 cause of data breaches.

rules.title: Do not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with unsanitized input
rules.description: dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React's XSS protection. If you must use it, sanitize the content with DOMPurify first. Never pass raw user input.

rules.title: All protected routes must verify authentication
rules.description: Every API route that accesses user data or performs mutations must verify the user's session or token before executing. No implicit trust.

examples.bad: export async function GET(req: Request) { const userId = req.headers.get('x-user-id'); return getUserData(userId); }
examples.good: export async function GET(req: Request) { const session = await getServerSession(authOptions); if (!session) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 }); return getUserData(session.user.id); }

rules.title: Verify resource ownership before returning data
rules.description: When fetching a resource by ID, always verify the authenticated user owns or has permission to access it. Never return a resource based on ID alone — this is an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR).

examples.good: const invoice = await db.invoices.findOne({ id: params.id, userId: session.user.id }); if (!invoice) return notFound();

rules.title: Do not log sensitive user data
rules.description: Passwords, tokens, full credit card numbers, SSNs, and raw PII must never appear in logs. Log IDs and non-sensitive metadata only.

rules.title: Auth tokens must use HttpOnly cookies
rules.description: Authentication tokens stored in localStorage or sessionStorage are vulnerable to XSS. Use HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies for session management.

examples.good: res.setHeader('Set-Cookie', serialize('token', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'strict' }));

rules.title: All external input must be validated and typed
rules.description: Any data entering the system from outside (HTTP requests, webhooks, file uploads, query params) must be validated against a schema before use. Use zod, yup, or equivalent.

examples.good: const schema = z.object({ amount: z.number().positive(), currency: z.enum(['USD', 'EUR']) }); const { amount, currency } = schema.parse(await req.json());

rules.title: Validate redirect URLs against an allowlist
rules.description: Redirecting to a user-supplied URL enables phishing attacks. Validate redirect targets against an allowlist of trusted domains or relative paths only.

examples.good: const redirectUrl = searchParams.get('redirect'); const ALLOWED = ['/dashboard', '/profile', '/settings']; return redirect(ALLOWED.includes(redirectUrl) ? redirectUrl : '/dashboard');

rules.title: Authentication endpoints must be rate limited
rules.description: Login, signup, password reset, and OTP endpoints must implement rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks. Use a token bucket or sliding window approach.

examples.bad: export async function POST(req: Request) { const { email, password } = await req.json(); return signIn(email, password); }
examples.good: const limiter = rateLimit({ max: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }); export async function POST(req: Request) { await limiter.check(req); const { email, password } = schema.parse(await req.json()); return signIn(email, password); }

rules.title: Avoid patterns that enable prototype pollution
rules.description: Merging or cloning objects from user input using Object.assign or spread without sanitization can pollute the Object prototype. Validate keys before merging.

examples.good: const safeInput = schema.parse(userInput); const config = Object.assign({}, defaults, safeInput);

rules.title: No dynamic requires or eval
rules.description: Dynamic require() calls and eval() with user-controlled input enable remote code execution. These patterns should never appear in application code.

examples.good: Import statically at the top of the file. Use a lookup map for dynamic behavior.
